description: Rh-AstroX is an innovative digital screening and health monitoring software tool designed for long-duration space missions. The platform analyzes complex blood profiles and genetic biomarkers, focusing specifically on astronauts with Rh-negative blood groups. By processing these unique biological variations, Rh-AstroX predicts the risk levels and progression of neurodegeneration, neurological shifts, and psychological impacts caused by prolonged deep-space exposure.
summary:
We developed R.A.D.A.R. (Rh-negative Astronaut Data, Analytics and Risk Profiling), a visual self-assessment and screening tool that helps astronauts track their mental, brain, and blood health during deep-space missions when a doctor is out of reach.
Space hazards like radiation and isolation heavily impact human health. Using daily check-ins—mood, sleep, stress, a 1-minute reaction test, heart rate, and blood pressure—R.A.D.A.R. calculates three simple scores: the Mental Health Risk Index (MHRI), Neurodegeneration Risk Index (NRI), and Blood Rise Index (BRI). It shows color-coded alerts, forecasts mental health four weeks ahead, triggers an urgent safety alert for self-harm thoughts, and compares Rh-positive and understudied Rh-negative profiles.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

R.A.D.A.R. (Rh-negative Astronaut Data, Analytics and Risk Profiling) is an AI-driven self-assessment and screening dashboard for astronauts on deep-space missions. Users enter daily check-ins—including mood, sleep, stress, a 1-minute reaction test (PVT), heart rate, and blood pressure—which an AI model processes to calculate three color-coded scores: Mental Health Risk Index (MHRI), Neurodegeneration Risk Index (NRI), and Blood Rise Index (BRI), alongside 4-week forecasts and daily decision-support guidance.

What benefits does it have?

During long missions to the Moon or Mars where immediate medical help is unavailable, R.A.D.A.R. empowers astronauts to independently monitor early warning signs across their mental, neurological, and blood health. It also includes an immediate safety protocol that triggers a red alert instructing the user to contact a flight surgeon or trusted crew member if self-harm thoughts are reported.

What is the intended impact of the project?

While R.A.D.A.R. is strictly an educational screening prototype rather than a clinical diagnostic tool, it establishes a vital foundation for future personalized space medicine. Once authentic Rh-negative astronaut data becomes available, this framework can evolve into a true clinical tool to safeguard vulnerable crew members on deep-space missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We developed the backend in Python with Flask and built an interactive, user-friendly frontend in HTML and CSS. We trained the predictive AI model on a structured 800-row dataset using Python data science libraries on standard computing hardware.

How is your project creative?

R.A.D.A.R. bridges psychology and aerospace hematology by introducing a unique "what-if" comparison slider between Rh-positive and understudied Rh-negative blood groups. Translating complex multi-variable telemetry into simple green, yellow, and red alerts makes advanced space health analytics accessible to non-specialists.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered NASA’s five primary spaceflight hazards—radiation, isolation, gravity changes, distance from Earth, and hostile environments—alongside astronaut age, gender, and mission duration. Because real Rh-negative astronaut data is not publicly available, we ethically calibrated our 800-row hypothetical dataset using validated biological and cognitive parameters from published NASA research (OSD-569 and Inspiration4 studies) while clearly stating its non-diagnostic scope.
